ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, H and I are on the same horizontal straight line, K is above, and J is on the right. Line segments KH, KI, KJ, JI, and the horizontal line HI form two adjacent triangles HIK and KIJ. In the figure, an exterior angle of 120° is marked at point H; at point K, the angle between KH and KI is 54°, and the angle between KI and KJ is 36°; what is required is the angle marked as 3 at point J. The pink arrows indicate that KH is parallel to JI. Reasoning: Because the 120° at point H is an exterior angle on the horizontal straight line, the interior angle of triangle HIK at point H is 180° − 120° = 60°. In triangle HIK, ∠HIK = 180° − 60° − 54° = 66°. Also because KH ∥ JI, and KI is a transversal, the angle formed by KI and JI at point I, ∠KIJ, is equal to the angle formed by KI and KH at point K, namely ∠KIJ = 54°. In triangle KIJ, the angle at point K is 36°, and the angle at point I is 54°, therefore ∠3 = 180° − 36° − 54° = 90°.

raw_record.question_text: If $\overline{K H}$ is parallel to $\overline{J I}$, find the measure of $\angle 3$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as two triangles sharing segment KI: H and I lie on a straight horizontal line, the 120° angle at H is exterior to triangle HIK, the angle at K between KH and KI is 54°, the angle at K between KI and KJ is 36°, and angle 3 is at J in triangle KIJ. From the straight line at H, the interior angle ∠KHI is 180° − 120° = 60°. In triangle HIK, compute ∠HIK = 180° − 60° − 54° = 66°. Use the given/text parallelism KH ∥ JI with KI as a transversal: the angle between KI and JI at I equals the angle between KI and KH at K, so ∠KIJ = 54° by alternate interior/corresponding angles. Then in triangle KIJ, ∠3 = 180° − 36° − 54° = 90°.

method.method_draft: Treat H-K-J-I as one quadrilateral. From the image, the angle at K of this quadrilateral is the sum of the two labeled angles, 54° + 36° = 90°. The marked 120° at H is exterior to the quadrilateral along the straight baseline, so the interior angle at H is 180° − 120° = 60°. Since KH ∥ JI, the side HI acts as a transversal; therefore the interior angle at I of quadrilateral HKJI is supplementary to the interior angle at H, so ∠HIJ = 180° − 60° = 120°. Now apply the quadrilateral angle sum: ∠3 = 360° − (60° + 90° + 120°) = 90°.
